matrices.label: Gather experimental pieces
matrices.level_1: Identify pieces the agent wrote while experimenting and recognize any notes describing changes, keeps, drops, or reasons.
matrices.level_2: Assemble the experimental pieces with the notes made after each one, keeping each note linked to the piece it describes.
matrices.level_3: Audit the collection for missing pieces, unpaired notes, or unclear links, and retrieve or flag gaps so the gathered material is reliable.
matrices.level_4: Design a traceable collection that preserves the sequence and relationships among experiments, layered versions, and reflection notes, so later review can follow how the work developed.

matrices.label: Gather layered pieces
matrices.level_1: Locate layered practice pieces when given clear experiment or version cues, and flag items that are missing or uncertain.
matrices.level_2: Gather the relevant layered pieces across the specified experiments, preserving their order and distinguishing each version from its earlier draft.
matrices.level_3: Curate the layered pieces independently, checking that each piece’s sequence of changes is traceable and surfacing gaps, duplicates, or unclear version links.
matrices.level_4: Design a reusable way to retrieve layered pieces as connected histories of revision, so new experiments can be added without losing how each version relates to the others.

matrices.label: Gather reflection notes
matrices.level_1: Locate reflection notes attached to practice pieces, identifying what the agent said it changed, kept, dropped, or why. Note when a piece has no visible reflection.
matrices.level_2: Gather the reflection notes for each experimental and layered piece, keeping each note linked to the piece it describes. Preserve the agent’s statements about changes, choices, and reasons without paraphrasing them as conclusions.
matrices.level_3: Verify that the gathered notes cover the available pieces and are attributed to the correct versions. Resolve misplaced or ambiguous notes where possible, and flag missing reflections rather than treating them as evidence.
matrices.level_4: Structure the reflection notes as a traceable record linked to the relevant pieces and their sequence of revisions. Adapt the links when pieces or notes are revised so the collection preserves how each reflection relates to the work it describes.

matrices.label: Assemble review corpus
matrices.level_1: Collects the agent’s practice pieces and reflection notes that belong to the review, recognizing which materials are relevant. Preserves each item in its original form.
matrices.level_2: Organizes the collected pieces into a coherent review set, pairing each piece with the notes made after it and keeping the sequence of practice clear. Uses consistent labels so each item can be found again.
matrices.level_3: Validates that the review corpus covers the intended practice and that pieces and reflection notes can be traced to one another. Flags missing or unpaired materials and makes the corpus’s limits clear before review begins.
matrices.level_4: Designs the corpus as a connected record of practice, preserving how pieces, iterations, and reflection notes relate across the body of work. Structures that record so later review can examine both individual pieces and the development linking them.

matrices.label: Compare across pieces
matrices.level_1: Describe visible similarities and differences between two practice pieces, pointing to the wording or structural moves that show each one.
matrices.level_2: Compare several pieces along a clear feature, citing examples of where the feature recurs and where the pieces diverge.
matrices.level_3: Analyze how similarities and differences persist or shift across the body of practice, using piece sequence and relevant reflection notes to support the comparison.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the comparisons into an account of how the practice pieces relate as a whole, showing how recurring elements and departures together trace the development of the agent’s voice.

matrices.label: Track repeated choices
matrices.level_1: Spot a choice that appears in more than one practice piece, identifying the pieces where it recurs.
matrices.level_2: Document each recurrence across the review corpus, noting where the choice appears and how it is expressed in each piece.
matrices.level_3: Analyze the pattern across the sequence of pieces, distinguishing steady recurrence from variation, gaps, or changes over time.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the tracked patterns into a map showing how repeated choices combine, overlap, or shift across the body of work, grounded in the pieces where they occur.

matrices.label: Name recurring choices
matrices.level_1: Recognize a choice that appears in more than one practice piece and point to the pieces where it occurs. Describe the repeated move in plain terms.
matrices.level_2: Compare instances across the practice pieces and give the recurring choice a clear, consistent name. Support the name with specific examples rather than treating similar wording alone as proof.
matrices.level_3: Analyze how a choice recurs across pieces even when its wording or form changes. Name the underlying move and cite examples that show both its variations and its continuity.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize several named recurring choices into a broader principle that explains how they work together across the practice pieces. Ground that principle in specific examples and show what it reveals about the agent’s emerging voice.

matrices.label: cross-reference intent notes
matrices.level_1: Locate an intent note for a practice piece and connect the choice it describes to a specific passage in that piece. Cite both sources.
matrices.level_2: Compare the stated intention with the piece’s actual choices, identifying where they align or diverge. Support each finding with citations from the note and the piece.
matrices.level_3: Trace an intended choice across pieces written in different styles, distinguishing what remains consistent from what changes with the style. Cite the relevant notes and passages.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize intent notes and cross-style evidence to infer the principle guiding a recurring choice. Test that interpretation against the pieces and surface contradictions between stated intentions and observed choices, with citations.

matrices.label: find the friction point where a repeat began
matrices.level_1: Spot a repeated choice in the practice pieces and point to where it appears. Mark a possible starting point without explaining what prompted it.
matrices.level_2: Trace the choice across pieces in sequence, comparing styles and using reflection notes to locate its first appearance or a change in its use. Distinguish that starting point from later instances that simply repeat it.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose where the repeat began by connecting the relevant piece, style shift, and reflection note. Explain what changed or became difficult there, and use the evidence to distinguish a deliberate choice from an old habit.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize what the friction point reveals about the broader relationship between chosen voice and default behavior across styles. Reframe the repeat and its beginning as parts of a general pattern, supported by evidence from the pieces and reflection notes.

matrices.label: identify baseline phrases
matrices.level_1: Spot phrases in a practice piece that read as familiar, stock, or readily reusable rather than specific to that piece. Quote the phrase as evidence.
matrices.level_2: Compare phrases across the gathered practice pieces and identify wording that recurs, citing the pieces where it appears. Include close variations when the phrasing changes slightly.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose recurring phrase patterns across different pieces, grouping exact repeats and meaningful variations when they serve the same phrasing move. Support each group with examples from the corpus.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize recurring phrases and their variations into the underlying phrase template they share. Show how examples across the pieces instantiate that template without treating every similar phrase as identical.

matrices.label: flag generic transitions
matrices.level_1: Flag generic transitions in a practice piece, pointing to the wording that makes the move feel formulaic or merely connects one part to the next.
matrices.level_2: Compare flagged transitions across the practice pieces and cite where the same generic bridge or phrasing recurs. Distinguish a one-off transition from a repeated pattern.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose whether a recurring generic transition reflects structural autopilot by checking it against the agent’s reflection notes about what it chose, kept, or changed. Cite the pieces and notes that support the flag.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the repeated transitions and their surrounding choices into a pattern that shows when generic bridges enter the agent’s writing. Use that pattern to refine what should be flagged as autopilot rather than treating every repeated transition as generic.

matrices.label: isolate systemic redundancies
matrices.level_1: Detect repeated wording, transitions, or structural moves across practice pieces, and point to the pieces where each repetition appears.
matrices.level_2: Analyze the repeated instances to group them by underlying move and distinguish a systemic redundancy from an isolated recurrence.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose how systemic redundancies recur across the corpus, using the pieces and reflection notes to trace their connection to default writing moves.
matrices.level_4: Reframe several redundancies as expressions of a shared underlying pattern, then propose a change to the writing approach that addresses the root without removing deliberate choices.

matrices.label: detect structural autopilot
matrices.level_1: Recognize a repeated structural move in the practice pieces, such as the same sequence, transition, or paragraph shape. Point to the pieces where it appears, without yet deciding whether it was deliberate or automatic.
matrices.level_2: Compare structural moves across the gathered pieces and establish which ones recur, citing their locations. Separate a pattern supported by multiple pieces from a one-off similarity.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose whether a recurring structure reflects an intentional choice or structural autopilot by weighing its appearances against reflection notes about what was changed, kept, or dropped. Explain what evidence supports that distinction, including cases where the pattern breaks.
matrices.level_4: Unify recurring structures, their exceptions, and reflection-note evidence into an account of the underlying template shaping the agent’s pieces. Show how apparently different repeated moves express the same default mechanism, distinguishing it from a deliberate voice principle.

matrices.label: Explain the repeat's function
matrices.level_1: Describe the apparent function of a recurring choice in a practice piece, pointing to the choice and the effect it seems to have. Keep the explanation close to what is visible in the example.
matrices.level_2: Explain how a repeated choice serves a recognizable purpose across several pieces, connecting its use to effects in the writing and to relevant reflection notes. Distinguish the function it seems to serve from merely noting that it recurs.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose how a recurring choice functions across the body of work, weighing stated intent, its effects, and examples where it was dropped or returned to. Explain whether the pattern appears to express a chosen preference or to operate as an unexamined habit, and support that reading with evidence.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the functions of recurring choices into a broader account of the voice taking shape, showing how intentional preferences and inherited habits interact across the pieces. Reframe the patterns as a principle that explains the body of work and guides which choices to preserve, revise, or reject next.

matrices.label: Assess future choice intent
matrices.level_1: Identify explicit statements in reflection notes about whether the agent intends to keep, change, or drop a recurring choice. Link each stated intention to the relevant practice piece.
matrices.level_2: Determine whether a recurring choice is intended for future use by comparing reflection notes with what the agent kept, changed, or dropped across pieces. Distinguish a stated future choice from a choice that merely recurs.
matrices.level_3: Evaluate how strongly the evidence supports the agent’s future intent, including cases where reflections conflict with later revisions or a dropped move returns. Explain what the pattern suggests about deliberate taste versus habit.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the assessed intentions across recurring choices into a coherent account of the voice the agent is choosing to develop. Show how that account follows from the pieces and notes, and distinguish deliberate commitments from habits that still need attention.

matrices.label: Distinguish taste from default
matrices.level_1: Identify a recurring choice in the practice pieces and classify it as a possible expression of taste or a possible default habit. Point to where it appears, without treating repetition alone as proof of intent.
matrices.level_2: Explain the classification by connecting the repeated choice to what the agent said it changed, kept, dropped, or why. Distinguish evidence of a deliberate preference from repetition that may simply carry over by habit.
matrices.level_3: Evaluate the choice across pieces and reflection notes, weighing stated intent against evidence such as rejected approaches, removed moves, or a repeat that returns. Judge whether it reflects taste, default, or a mixture, and qualify the judgment where the evidence is unclear.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the patterns into a principle that explains how deliberate preferences and old habits interact across the agent’s voice. Use that principle to distinguish choices the agent wants to carry forward from defaults it may want to change.

matrices.label: quote recurring wording
matrices.level_1: Identify wording that appears more than once and quote it exactly from a practice piece, preserving the original words and punctuation.
matrices.level_2: Compare practice pieces and quote matching wording from each occurrence, identifying the piece each quotation comes from.
matrices.level_3: Trace recurring wording across the corpus, quoting each occurrence accurately and distinguishing exact matches from similar but changed phrasing.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize a citation trail that shows how wording persists or changes across practice pieces, quoting the relevant forms and linking each to its source without treating variations as exact matches.

matrices.label: cite supporting pieces
matrices.level_1: Identify a practice piece that supports a stated observation about the agent’s voice, naming it clearly enough to locate in the review corpus.
matrices.level_2: Select and cite multiple pieces that directly support a recurring choice, linking each citation to the specific observation it backs.
matrices.level_3: Validate the evidence for a voice claim by citing pieces from across the corpus and noting when the cited examples do not fully support its scope.
matrices.level_4: Reframe the citations as an evidence path that shows how a choice persists or changes across pieces, making clear what broader voice claim the examples can—and cannot—establish.

matrices.label: cite reflection notes
matrices.level_1: Locate reflection notes that mention a choice made while writing a practice piece, and quote or identify the relevant passage. Make clear which piece the note belongs to.
matrices.level_2: Connect a reflection-note citation to the specific choice it explains in its piece, using the note’s wording as evidence rather than paraphrasing it as fact. Include enough context to show what the agent said it changed, kept, dropped, or why.
matrices.level_3: Corroborate a recurring choice with citations from reflection notes attached to multiple pieces. Compare what the notes say about the choice, and preserve differences or contradictions instead of treating every mention as identical.
matrices.level_4: Integrate reflection-note citations across the practice corpus to show how the agent’s stated reasons for a repeated choice develop or persist. Distinguish what the notes support about deliberate voice from what remains an interpretation of habit.

matrices.label: separate evidence from interpretation
matrices.level_1: Identify which statements are directly present in a practice piece or reflection note and which are interpretations about them. Point to the text that makes the difference visible.
matrices.level_2: Separate each interpretation from its supporting evidence by quoting or citing the relevant pieces and notes. Label what the source says and what you infer from it.
matrices.level_3: Scrutinize interpretations against evidence across the corpus, including examples that complicate or contradict them. Qualify conclusions when the cited pieces support only part of the claim.
matrices.level_4: Model the path from cited evidence to interpretation across the practice pieces and notes, making the scope and limits of each inference explicit. Build an account of recurring choices that readers can trace back to the source without mistaking the interpretation for what the pieces literally say.

matrices.label: tally repeated choices
matrices.level_1: Count clear instances of a named choice in a piece or small set of pieces, recording a straightforward total.
matrices.level_2: Tally each named choice across the practice pieces, keeping per-piece counts distinct from the corpus total.
matrices.level_3: Validate tallies when instances are ambiguous or vary in form by applying a consistent inclusion rule and revising affected counts.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize tallies for distinct surface forms that express the same underlying choice, reporting a consolidated count while preserving the component counts.

matrices.label: calculate appearance rate
matrices.level_1: Compute a basic appearance rate for a named choice from supplied counts by dividing the number of pieces containing it by the total number of pieces. State the numerator, denominator, and resulting rate.
matrices.level_2: Calculate appearance rates by locating a named choice across the review corpus, counting the pieces where it occurs, and dividing by the corpus size. Cite the pieces that support the count and report the result consistently as a fraction or percentage.
matrices.level_3: Validate rates across patterns or subsets of the practice pieces, stating what counts as an appearance and which pieces form each denominator. Distinguish a choice appearing in a piece from multiple instances within that piece, and flag limits that could make the rates misleading.
matrices.level_4: Design an appearance-rate measure suited to the comparison when corpus sizes or piece groupings differ, making its unit and denominator explicit. Show how the measure supports a fair comparison across the practice pieces and how an alternative definition would change the conclusion.

matrices.label: rank recurring patterns
matrices.level_1: Recognize choices that recur across the practice pieces and distinguish those that appear more or less often by inspection.
matrices.level_2: Order recurring choices by tallying their appearances across the corpus, citing counts and assigning equal counts the same rank.
matrices.level_3: Validate the ordering against the full set of pieces, using appearance rates when patterns have different opportunities to occur and flagging close counts or ties that limit confidence.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the validated rankings into a frequency hierarchy that shows whether choices form a dominant core, distinct tiers, or near-equal clusters, grounding each placement in counts or rates.

matrices.label: Track dropped wording
matrices.level_1: Locate wording present in an earlier practice piece but absent from a later version, quoting the text and identifying both pieces. Mark the omission without assuming why it occurred.
matrices.level_2: Trace omitted wording across multiple practice pieces, recording each appearance and absence so isolated edits can be distinguished from recurring omissions. Include wording that later returns as evidence of a different pattern.
matrices.level_3: Validate claims of dropped or returning wording against the relevant versions and reflection notes, citing evidence for each claim. Identify when the record is incomplete or ambiguous, and qualify conclusions accordingly.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the well-supported omissions and returns across the corpus into an account of which wording patterns consistently fall away and which do not. Ground that account in cited pieces and make its evidential limits clear.

matrices.label: Track removed moves
matrices.level_1: Identify a move that a piece or reflection note explicitly says was removed, replaced, or crossed out. Record the piece and the supporting evidence.
matrices.level_2: Trace documented removals of the same move across practice pieces and reflection notes, linking each occurrence to its source. Keep separate removal events distinct rather than merging similar edits.
matrices.level_3: Assess how strongly the pieces and notes support each claimed removal or return, distinguishing explicit evidence from indirect clues and mere absence. Mark uncertainty where the record does not establish what happened.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the evidence into a corpus-wide history of removed moves, showing when each move was dropped, returned, or documented again. Preserve the strength and source of each link so the overall account does not present gaps as proof.

matrices.label: Track rejected approaches
matrices.level_1: Record approaches the agent explicitly rejects in a piece or reflection note, citing the supporting evidence. Keep documented rejections separate from approaches that are merely absent.
matrices.level_2: Trace each documented rejection across the practice pieces and reflection notes, noting where it appears, recurs, or is contradicted by a later return. Distinguish a single recorded instance from evidence found across multiple pieces.
matrices.level_3: Assess how strongly the evidence supports classifying an approach as consistently rejected, weighing the specificity and corroboration of the records against any counterexamples. Calibrate the claim to the evidence, without inferring why the agent rejected it.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize well-supported rejections and counterexamples into a coherent map of approaches consistently excluded versus those rejected only in particular experiments. Show how the cited evidence establishes those boundaries without treating each rejection as an isolated event.

matrices.label: Flag drops that return
matrices.level_1: Recognize a move or wording marked as dropped when it appears again in a later practice piece. Point to the reflection note and the piece as evidence of the return.
matrices.level_2: Trace a candidate return across the reflection notes and practice pieces, checking that the later instance is the same move rather than a superficial resemblance. Cite the sequence showing when it was dropped and where it reappeared.
matrices.level_3: Assess how firmly the evidence supports a return by checking whether the drop is clearly documented and the later instance is identifiable in the piece. Cite both sources and distinguish a confirmed return from an ambiguous echo.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize confirmed and uncertain returns across multiple pieces to reveal which kinds of recurrence are consistently supported by the evidence. Cite examples and explain how the cross-piece pattern differs from an isolated or ambiguous instance.
